subject: [hw] V40 -> IV: your mmap sequence explained; MAP_FIXED cannot reach the device through the frozen mmap callback
body:
Late answer to your V40 question (14 calls, the 0x88000000 mapping and the vsi address) - the model-side facts, no request unless M-d needs the second part:

1) offset 0x88000000 is MAP_SHMEM_COMMIT_BASE: mtk_vcu.c:100-113 has ALLOC 0x80000000 and COMMIT (ALLOC + 0x8000000) = 0x88000000, both 0x80000 long. vcu_mmu_map() maps the SAME 0x80000 DMEM in both cases; on the phone they are two vmas, and only the COMMIT one sets DMEM0_VMA = vma->vm_start (:1707-1711). Our device callback returns a guest address chosen by the model, so both calls return dmem_guest = 0x40000000 and 0x40001000 + delta resolves to the same bytes. That is not two mappings of one interval in the guest: the second call simply returns the same address and the caller overwrites its own vma bookkeeping. len=0x3f0 is just the callers length (remap_shmem copies a .data segment in); the model accepts any length <= 0x80000 in that range.

2) The model cannot honour mmap addr/MAP_FIXED at all: include/n2elf.h struct n2vfs_dev.mmap(ctx, cpu, len, prot, offset, err) has no addr argument, and V33s n2vfs_mmap does `(void)addr;` and returns the devices address (shim/n2vfs.c:807-825). So "V40 ignored addr" is the frozen interface, not a model choice. If M-d needs the COMMIT mapping placed at vpuds requested address (vma->vm_start semantics, opus-venc reports reaching M-d with such a fix in a /tmp copy), the change is one of:
   a) add a uint32_t addr argument to n2vfs_dev.mmap (frozen header -> hw-lead, and V33s caller passes it), then V40 maps the DMEM pages at that guest address when it is free, or
   b) a model-side API n2vcu_dmem_set_base(vcu, guest) that V33/IV call before the COMMIT mmap, with the device then returning that address for it.
I have not added either unilaterally because (a) edits a frozen header and (b) needs a caller I do not own. Say which the lead wants and I will implement the V40 half immediately (both are small; the DMA/VMEM tables do not change).

3) The reported vcu_inst_addr 0x4010ceb0 is 0x10ceb0 past dmem_guest and past the 0x80000 DMEM, so it is not a DMEM address in this model and not one the kernel would accept either (vcu_mapping_dm_addr: d_off > len -> NULL). That remains the V34/ION vs heap question; V40s map_dm_addr correctly rejects it.

Also: the GET_LOG re-measure I posted stands (1 entry into the ioctl per 5 s run, log_gets=0; was 805506). No change from this note.
